To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the water vapor continuum in the near infrared is a strong absorber, that its strength is not well understood, that the absorption is not well described by current models, and that its strength is wavelength dependent.

the continuum absorption in the water vapour band at 1.4 m is not well described in the current line-by-line radiative transfer codes, but that it can be described by an empirical absorption model based on the HITRAN 2016 line parameters and the new continuum absorption data.

the water vapor continuum is not a single continuum but a collection of overlapping continua, and that the absorption of the water vapor continuum depends strongly on temperature, pressure, and wavelength, and on the presence of foreign gases.
